To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single phase multilevel ac–dc– ac converter with a reduced number (six) of controlled switches has been proposed.

the proposed converters have the following advantages compared with the conventional converter: 1) the number of controlled switches is reduced by 25%; 2) the dc-link volt ages are balanced and regulated by the control; 3) the grid power factor is maintained at unity; 4) the output voltage is sinusoidal; 5) the voltage harmonic distortion is low; 6) the system is robust; and 7) the system can operate with different load conditions.

a single-phase ac–ac converter is presented with a reduced number and a reduced rating of controlled switches, which is able to feed a single-phase load voltage with sinusoids with constant frequency and amplitude and to operate with a sinusoidal grid current.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a novel single-phase ac–ac converter with a reduced number (six) of switches and with the development of a control system that allows the converter to operate as a UPS and UPQC for nonregenerative systems.
the analysis, design, and implementation of a single-phase multilevel ac–dc– ac converter for power conditioning and power factor correction.
a new family of unidirectional single–phase ac–dc– ac converters with a reduced switching frequency, which is composed of two three–leg converters connected in series and fed by a single dc source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed converters can operate as uninterruptible and unified power quality conditioning systems for nonregenerative ac–dc–dc–ac applications with reduced number of controlled semiconductor switches.
the proposed topologies have better performance than the conventional one.

the proposed topologies offer the advantages of the conventional single-phase multilevel converters, such as the capability to feed the load with sinusoidal voltaged with constant amplitude and a unity power factor, and the possibility to operate in the whole voltage range of the grid, while the number of switches to be controlled is reduced by half.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we proposed two unidirectional ac–dc– ac converters based on three-leg converter with a reduced number semiconductor devices.
the proposed converters are able to operate with unity power factor and sinusoidal load voltages and currents.

we have proposed and implemented a novel single-phase multilevel converter with a reduced number (six) of controlled switches, which allows us to feed the ac load with sinusoidal voltaged with a constant amplitude and frequency, and to operate with a high power quality factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed converters have the following advantages compared to the conventional ones: (i) a reduced number of switches, (ii) a reduced number and complexity of the control system, (iii) the same capability to operate with sinusoidally shaped load and grid voltage, and (iv) a lower semiconductor losses.
we have proposed two single-phase multilevel converters that have a reduced number of switches and are able to feed the load with a constant voltage and sinusoidal current.

the proposed topologies can be used in nonregenerative applications, such as uninterruptible supplies and unified power conditioning systems, with the same performance as the conventional topology with a reduced number and cost of controlled switches.
